claim: The concept of chemoconnectome (CCT) covers the entire chemical transmission between neurons and target cells in an organism.
source: We have previously proposed the concept of chemoconnectome (CCT) to cover the entire chemical transmission between neurons and target cells in an organism and created tools for studying it (CCTomics) by targeting all genes related to the CCT in Drosophila.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a definition of the CCT concept.

claim: CCTomics tools have been created by targeting all genes related to the CCT in Drosophila.
source: We have previously proposed the concept of chemoconnectome (CCT) to cover the entire chemical transmission between neurons and target cells in an organism and created tools for studying it (CCTomics) by targeting all genes related to the CCT in Drosophila.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a previous accomplishment by the authors.

claim: Three strategies for conditional CCT gene targeting have been created: GFP RNA interference, Flp-out, and CRISPR/Cas9 technologies.
source: Here we have created lines targeting the CCT in a conditional manner after modifying GFP RNA interference, Flp-out, and CRISPR/Cas9 technologies.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as the main methodological contribution.

claim: All three conditional targeting strategies have been validated to be highly effective.
source: All three strategies have been validated to be highly effective, with the best using chromatin-peptide fused Cas9 variants and scaffold optimized sgRNAs.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a result of validation experiments.

claim: The best conditional targeting strategy uses chromatin-peptide fused Cas9 variants and scaffold optimized sgRNAs.
source: All three strategies have been validated to be highly effective, with the best using chromatin-peptide fused Cas9 variants and scaffold optimized sgRNAs.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a comparative result.

claim: 43 CCT genes are present in clock neurons.
source: As a proof of principle, we conducted a comprehensive intersection analysis of CCT genes expression profiles in the clock neurons, uncovering 43 CCT genes present in clock neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a result of intersection analysis.

claim: Loss of the neuropeptide CNMa in two posterior dorsal clock neurons (DN1ps) causes advanced morning activity.
source: Specific elimination of each from clock neurons revealed that loss of the neuropeptide CNMa in two posterior dorsal clock neurons (DN1ps) or its receptor (CNMaR) caused advanced morning activity, indicating a suppressive role of CNMa-CNMaR on morning anticipation, opposite to the promoting role of PDF-PDFR on morning anticipation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a result of specific elimination experiments.

claim: Loss of CNMaR causes advanced morning activity.
source: Specific elimination of each from clock neurons revealed that loss of the neuropeptide CNMa in two posterior dorsal clock neurons (DN1ps) or its receptor (CNMaR) caused advanced morning activity, indicating a suppressive role of CNMa-CNMaR on morning anticipation, opposite to the promoting role of PDF-PDFR on morning anticipation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a result of specific elimination experiments.

claim: CNMa-CNMaR has a suppressive role on morning anticipation.
source: Specific elimination of each from clock neurons revealed that loss of the neuropeptide CNMa in two posterior dorsal clock neurons (DN1ps) or its receptor (CNMaR) caused advanced morning activity, indicating a suppressive role of CNMa-CNMaR on morning anticipation, opposite to the promoting role of PDF-PDFR on morning anticipation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: PDF-PDFR has a promoting role on morning anticipation.
source: Specific elimination of each from clock neurons revealed that loss of the neuropeptide CNMa in two posterior dorsal clock neurons (DN1ps) or its receptor (CNMaR) caused advanced morning activity, indicating a suppressive role of CNMa-CNMaR on morning anticipation, opposite to the promoting role of PDF-PDFR on morning anticipation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a comparison to the CNMa-CNMaR role.

claim: CNMa-CNMaR and PDF-PDFR signaling have an antagonistic relationship in regulating morning anticipation.
source: These results demonstrate the effectiveness of conditional CCTomics and its tools created here and establish an antagonistic relationship between CNMa-CNMaR and PDF-PDFR signaling in regulating morning anticipation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the experimental results.

claim: CCTomics overcomes limitations of previous circuit dissection strategies by allowing for behavioral screening of CCT genes and accurate labeling or manipulation of corresponding neurons.
source: CCTomics overcomes limitations of previous strategies by allowing for behavioral screening of CCT genes and accurate labeling or manipulation of corresponding neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an advantage of CCTomics.

claim: Knockout of some CCT genes can be lethal during development.
source: However, it is still limited in that knockout of some CCT genes can be lethal during development and that CCT genes may function differently in different neurons, which require a cell-type-specific manipulation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a limitation of CCTomics.

claim: CCT genes may function differently in different neurons.
source: However, it is still limited in that knockout of some CCT genes can be lethal during development and that CCT genes may function differently in different neurons, which require a cell-type-specific manipulation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a limitation of CCTomics.

claim: Libraries of transgenic RNAi flies covering almost the entire fly genome have been established.
source: Libraries of transgenic RNAi flies covering almost the entire fly genome have been established (Ni et al., 2011; Perkins et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: The widespread use of CRISPR/Cas9 in Drosophila somatic gene manipulation began in 2014.
source: The widespread use of CRIPSR/Cas9 in Drosophila somatic gene manipulation began in 2014 (Xue et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: tRNA-flanking sgRNAs enable multiple sgRNAs to mature in a single transcript.
source: Later, tRNA-flanking sgRNAs was designed and applied, which enabled multiple sgRNAs to mature in a single transcript (Xie et al., 2015), accelerating the application of this strategy in conditional gene manipulation in flies with impressive efficiency (Delventhal et al., 2019; Port and Bullock, 2016; Port et al., 2020; Schlichting et al., 2019; Schlichting et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Libraries of UAS-sgRNA targeting kinases have been established.
source: Additionally, libraries of UAS-sgRNA targeting kinases (Port et al., 2020) and GPCRs Schlichting et al., 2022 have been established, but no sgRNA libraries covering all the CCT genes exist yet.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Libraries of UAS-sgRNA targeting GPCRs have been established.
source: Additionally, libraries of UAS-sgRNA targeting kinases (Port et al., 2020) and GPCRs Schlichting et al., 2022 have been established, but no sgRNA libraries covering all the CCT genes exist yet.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: No sgRNA libraries covering all the CCT genes exist.
source: Additionally, libraries of UAS-sgRNA targeting kinases (Port et al., 2020) and GPCRs Schlichting et al., 2022 have been established, but no sgRNA libraries covering all the CCT genes exist yet.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a gap in existing resources.

claim: The efficiency of CRISPR/Cas9 has not been validated systematically in the Drosophila nervous system.
source: The efficiency of CRISPR/Cas9 has not been validated systematically in the Drosophila nervous system.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a gap in existing knowledge.

claim: Drosophila shows enhanced activity before the light is turned on and off in a light–dark (LD) cycle, referred to as morning and evening anticipations.
source: The rhythmic locomotor behavior of Drosophila, for instance, shows enhanced activity before the light is turned on and off in a light–dark (LD) cycle, referred to as morning and evening anticipations, respectively (Collins et al., 2005; Helfrich Förster, 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Under 12 hr dark–12 hr dark (DD) conditions, Drosophila activities peak regularly about every 24 hr.
source: Under 12 hr dark–12 hr dark (DD) conditions, the activities peak regularly about every 24 hr (Konopka and Benzer, 1971).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Approximately 150 clock neurons, circadian output neurons, and extra-clock electrical oscillators (xCEOs) coordinate Drosophila circadian behaviors.
source: Approximately 150 clock neurons, circadian output neurons, and extra-clock electrical oscillators (xCEOs) coordinate Drosophila circadian behaviors (Dubowy and Sehgal, 2017; Tang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: The regulation of morning and evening anticipations is primarily mediated by four pairs of sLNvs expressing pigment dispersing factor (PDF), six pairs of LNds and the fifth s-LNv.
source: The regulation of morning and evening anticipations, the most prominent features in the LD condition, is primarily mediated by four pairs of sLNvs expressing pigment dispersing factor (PDF), six pairs of LNds and the fifth s-LNv (Grima et al., 2004; Rieger et al., 2006; Stoleru et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Pdf and Pdfr mutants show an advanced evening activity peak and no morning anticipation.
source: At the molecular level, Pdf and Pdf receptor (PDFR) are well known, with their mutants showing an advanced evening activity peak and no morning anticipation (Hyun et al., 2005; Lear et al., 2005; Renn et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: AstC/AstC-R2 and neuropeptide F (NPF) and its receptor (NPFR) modulate evening activities.
source: Other neuropeptides and their receptors, including AstC/AstC-R2 and neuropeptide F (NPF) and its receptor (NPFR), have also been reported to modulate evening activities (Díaz et al., 2019; He et al., 2013; Hermann et al., 2012), while CCHa1/CCHa1-R and Dh31 regulate morning activities (Fujiwara et al., 2018; Goda et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: CCHa1/CCHa1-R and Dh31 regulate morning activities.
source: Other neuropeptides and their receptors, including AstC/AstC-R2 and neuropeptide F (NPF) and its receptor (NPFR), have also been reported to modulate evening activities (Díaz et al., 2019; He et al., 2013; Hermann et al., 2012), while CCHa1/CCHa1-R and Dh31 regulate morning activities (Fujiwara et al., 2018; Goda et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: No advanced morning activity phenotype has been reported in flies to date.
source: To date, no advanced morning activity phenotype has been reported in flies.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a gap in existing knowledge.

claim: Pan-neuronal expression of shRNAGFP or flipase almost completely eliminated GFP signals of target genes.
source: Immunofluorescent imaging showed that constitutive expression of shRNAGFP (Figure 1B–D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–I) or flipase (Figure 1E–G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1J–U) almost completely eliminated GFP signals of target genes, indicating high efficiency.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing elimination of GFP signals.

claim: Knocking out at the adult stage using hsFLP driven Flp-out resulted in the elimination of most, though not all, GFP signals.
source: Knocking out at the adult stage using either hsFLP driven Flp-out (Golic and Lindquist, 1989; Figure 1H–J) or neural (elav-Switch) driven shRNAGFP (Nicholson et al., 2008; Osterwalder et al., 2001; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–I) also resulted in the elimination of most, though not all, GFP signals.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations and supported by figures.

claim: Control group of CCTEGFP.FRT; elav-Switch/UAS-shRNAGFP flies fed with solvent (ethanol) showed obvious decreased GFP compared with UAS-shRNAGFP/CCTEGFP.FRT flies fed with RU486.
source: Notably, control group of CCTEGFP.FRT; elav-Switch/UAS-shRNAGFP flies fed with solvent (ethanol) showed obvious decreased GFP (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B, E, and H) compared with UAS-shRNAGFP/CCTEGFP.FRT flies fed with RU486 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, D, and G), indicating leaky expression of elav-Switch or shRNAGFP.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures.

claim: There is leaky expression of elav-Switch or shRNAGFP.
source: Notably, control group of CCTEGFP.FRT; elav-Switch/UAS-shRNAGFP flies fed with solvent (ethanol) showed obvious decreased GFP (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B, E, and H) compared with UAS-shRNAGFP/CCTEGFP.FRT flies fed with RU486 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, D, and G), indicating leaky expression of elav-Switch or shRNAGFP.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Ablation of nAChRβ2 in the nervous system dramatically decreased sleep of flies, mirroring the nAChRβ2 knockout phenotype.
source: Ablation of nAChRβ2 in the nervous system dramatically decreased sleep of flies, mirroring the nAChRβ2 knockout phenotype (Figure 1K and L).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing sleep data.

claim: Expression of in-frame fused EGFP-labeled CCT genes highly co-localized with signals revealed by immunocytochemistry.
source: Expression of in-frame fused EGFP-labeled CCT genes highly co-localized with signals revealed by immunocytochemistry (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–I), allowing direct examination of gene expression without amplification, which is different from the GAL4/UAS binary system.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing co-localization.

claim: cCCT lines including CapaEGFP.FRT, ChATEGFP.FRT, and EhEGFP.FRT were viable, whereas their CCT mutants were lethal.
source: We then checked the viability of cCCT lines and found that cCCT lines including CapaEGFP.FRT, ChATEGFP.FRT, and EhEGFP.FRT were viable, whereas their CCT mutants were lethal.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an observation from viability checks.

claim: Gad1EGFP.FRT, GluRIIDEGFP.FRT, and CapaREGFP.FRT were lethal as their CCT mutants were.
source: Gad1EGFP.FRT, GluRIIDEGFP.FRT, and CapaREGFP.FRT were still lethal as their CCT mutants were (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an observation from viability checks.

claim: Some of the cCCT knockin flies may functionally affect corresponding genes, which are not suitable for conditional gene manipulation.
source: This indicates that some of the cCCT knockin flies may functionally affect corresponding genes, which are not suitable for conditional gene manipulation.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an interpretation of the viability data.

claim: An optimized sgRNA scaffold 'E+F' (E, stem extension; F, A-U flip) facilitates Cas9-sgRNA complex formation and gene knockout efficiency.
source: We also adopted an optimized sgRNA scaffold 'E+F' (E, stem extension; F, A-U flip) (Chen et al., 2013), which facilitates Cas9-sgRNA complex formation and gene knockout efficiency (Dang et al., 2015; Poe et al., 2019; Zhao et al., 2016), to all sgRNAs to improve gene knockout efficiency.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to support the claim.

claim: Three sgRNAs were selected for each CCT gene with the highest predicted efficiency and no predicted off-target effect.
source: To balance efficiency and off-target effect, we selected three sgRNAs for each CCT gene with the highest predicted efficiency and no predicted off-target effect based on previously reported models (Chu et al., 2016; Doench et al., 2014; Graf et al., 2019; Gratz et al., 2014; Heigwer et al., 2014; Stemmer et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2015; see Supplementary file 3 and 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to support the methodology.

claim: Sanger sequencing showed that indels were present exactly at the Cas9 cleavage sites.
source: Sanger sequencing showed that indels were present exactly at the Cas9 cleavage sites (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing sequencing results.

claim: Targeting by Cas9.HC/sgRNADh31 eliminated most but not all of the GFP signal in Dh31EGFP.FRT.
source: Targeting by Cas9.HC/sgRNADh31 eliminated most but not all of the GFP signal in Dh31EGFP.FRT (Figure 2B–D), whereas all anti-PDF signals were eliminated by Cas9.HC/sgRNApdf (Figure 2E–G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing GFP signals.

claim: All anti-PDF signals were eliminated by Cas9.HC/sgRNApdf.
source: Targeting by Cas9.HC/sgRNADh31 eliminated most but not all of the GFP signal in Dh31EGFP.FRT (Figure 2B–D), whereas all anti-PDF signals were eliminated by Cas9.HC/sgRNApdf (Figure 2E–G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing anti-PDF signals.

claim: Pan-neuronal knockout of Pdfr resulted in a tendency toward advanced evening activity and weaker morning anticipation compared to control flies.
source: Pan-neuronal knockout of Pdfr resulted in a tendency toward advanced evening activity and weaker morning anticipation compared to control flies (Figure 2H and I), which is similar to Pdfr-attpKO flies.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing activity profiles.

claim: There was no significant sleep decrease in cKO flies when C-cCCTomics was applied to manipulate nAChRβ2 or nAChRa2.
source: Furthermore, there was no significant sleep decrease in these cKO flies (Figure 2J and K) when we applied C-cCCTomics to manipulate nAChRβ2 or nAChRa2.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing sleep data.

claim: C-cCCTomics (with Cas9.HC) achieved a relatively high gene knockout efficiency, but it was not effective enough for all genes.
source: Taken together, C-cCCTomics (with Cas9.HC) achieved a relatively high gene knockout efficiency, but it was not effective enough for all genes.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a summary of the Cas9.HC efficiency.

claim: Cas9.M9 was fused with HMGN1 at the N-terminus and HMGB1 at its C-terminus with GGSGP linker.
source: We fused a chromatin-modulating peptide (Ding et al., 2019), HMGN1 (high mobility group nucleosome binding domain 1), at the N-terminus of Cas9 and HMGB1 (high mobility group protein B1) at its C-terminus with GGSGP linker, termed Cas9.M9 (Figure 3A, 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation and supported by a figure showing the structure.

claim: Cas9.M6 was modified with HMGN1 at the N-terminus and an undefined peptide (UDP) at the C-terminus.
source: We also obtained a modified Cas9.M6 with HMGN1 at the N-terminus and an undefined peptide (UDP) at the C-terminus (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a figure showing the structure.

claim: Cas9.M0 was created by replacing the STARD linker between Cas9 and NLS in Cas9.HC with the GGSGP linker.
source: We replaced the STARD linker between Cas9 and NLS in Cas9.HC with the GGSGP linker (Zhao et al., 2016), termed Cas9.M0 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation and supported by a figure showing the structure.

claim: Unmodified Cas9.HC/sgRNAple only achieved 69.58 ± 3.04% knockout efficiency.
source: By counting anti-TH-positive neurons in the brain (anterior view) after targeting by Cas9/sgRNAple, we found that unmodified Cas9.HC/sgRNAple only achieved 69.58 ± 3.04% (n = 5) knockout efficiency (Figure 3G, K, and L), while Cas9.M6/sgRNAple and Cas9.M9/sgRNAple significantly improved efficiency to 87.53 ± 3.06% (n = 7) and 97.19 ± 2.15% (n = 8), respectively (Figure 3I–L).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing neuron counts.

claim: Cas9.M6/sgRNAple significantly improved efficiency to 87.53 ± 3.06%.
source: By counting anti-TH-positive neurons in the brain (anterior view) after targeting by Cas9/sgRNAple, we found that unmodified Cas9.HC/sgRNAple only achieved 69.58 ± 3.04% (n = 5) knockout efficiency (Figure 3G, K, and L), while Cas9.M6/sgRNAple and Cas9.M9/sgRNAple significantly improved efficiency to 87.53 ± 3.06% (n = 7) and 97.19 ± 2.15% (n = 8), respectively (Figure 3I–L).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing neuron counts.

claim: Cas9.M9/sgRNAple significantly improved efficiency to 97.19 ± 2.15%.
source: By counting anti-TH-positive neurons in the brain (anterior view) after targeting by Cas9/sgRNAple, we found that unmodified Cas9.HC/sgRNAple only achieved 69.58 ± 3.04% (n = 5) knockout efficiency (Figure 3G, K, and L), while Cas9.M6/sgRNAple and Cas9.M9/sgRNAple significantly improved efficiency to 87.53 ± 3.06% (n = 7) and 97.19 ± 2.15% (n = 8), respectively (Figure 3I–L).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing neuron counts.

claim: Cas9.M6 and Cas9.M9 demonstrated significantly higher gene disruption efficiency compared to the unmodified Cas9.HC, achieving average efficiencies of 87.51% ± 2.24% and 89.59% ± 2.39% for Cas9.M6 and Cas9.M9, respectively, in contrast to 70.72% ± 3.82% for Cas9.HC.
source: Cas9.M6 and Cas9.M9 demonstrated significantly higher gene disruption efficiency compared to the unmodified Cas9.HC, achieving average efficiencies of 87.51% ± 2.24% and 89.59% ± 2.39% for Cas9.M6 and Cas9.M9, respectively, in contrast to 70.72% ± 3.82% for Cas9.HC. (Figure 3M, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing gene disruption efficiency.

claim: Both Cas9.M6 and Cas9.M9 exhibited lower mRNA levels than Cas9.HC under the experiment condition.
source: To rule out the possibility of the observed variations in gene disruption efficiency being attributed to differential Cas9 expression levels, we quantified the Cas9 expression levels and noted that both Cas9.M6 and Cas9.M9 exhibited lower mRNA levels than Cas9.HC under the experiment condition (Figure 3N).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a figure showing expression levels.

claim: The single-site mutation rates varied from 5.81% to 43.47% for Cas9.HC, 22.40% to 53.54% for Cas9.M6, and 19.90% to 63.57% for Cas9.M9.
source: The single-site mutation rates varied from 5.81% to 43.47% for Cas9.HC, 22.40% to 53.54% for Cas9.M6, and 19.90% to 63.57% for Cas9.M9 (Figure 3P, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing mutation rates.

claim: Both Cas9.M6 and Cas9.M9 displayed elevated efficiency compared to Cas9.HC, with Cas9.M9 exhibiting the highest mutagenesis proficiency.
source: The findings indicated that both Cas9.M6 and Cas9.M9 displayed elevated efficiency compared to Cas9.HC, with Cas9.M9 exhibiting the highest mutagenesis proficiency.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a summary of the efficiency data.

claim: Pan-neuronal knocking out of nAChRβ2 or nAChRa2 by Cas9.M9/sgRNA showed significant sleep decrease, which was similar to their mutants.
source: Pan-neuronal knocking out of nAChRβ2 or nAChRa2 by Cas9.M9/sgRNA showed significant sleep decrease, which was similar to their mutants (Figure 3Q, R; Dai et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation and supported by figures showing sleep data.

claim: 43 out of 148 analyzed CCT genes were expressed in circadian neurons.
source: With the Flp-out or split-LexA intersection strategy (Figure 4A and B), we found 43 out of 148 analyzed CCT genes expressed in circadian neurons (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplements 1–2, and Supplementary files 4 and 5 ).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing expression profiles.

claim: 23 CCT genes were expressed in DN1s, 20 in DN2s, 22 in DN3s, 28 in LNds, 14 in l-LNvs, 12 in s-LNvs, 5 in fifth s-LNv, and 3 in LPNs, with a total of 127 gene subsets.
source: In all eight subsets of clock neurons, 23 CCT genes were expressed in DN1s, 20 in DN2s, 22 in DN3s, 28 in LNds, 14 in l-LNvs, 12 in s-LNvs, 5 in fifth s-LNv, and 3 in LPNs, with a total of 127 gene subsets.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a summary of the expression analysis.

claim: The expression of CCHa1 in two DN1s was confirmed.
source: Initially, we confirmed the expression of CCHa1 in two DN1s (Fujiwara et al., 2018), sNFP in four s-LNvs and two LNds (Johard et al., 2009), and Trissin in two LNds (Ma et al., 2021), aligning with previous findings.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to support the claim.

claim: The expression of sNFP in four s-LNvs and two LNds was confirmed.
source: Initially, we confirmed the expression of CCHa1 in two DN1s (Fujiwara et al., 2018), sNFP in four s-LNvs and two LNds (Johard et al., 2009), and Trissin in two LNds (Ma et al., 2021), aligning with previous findings.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to support the claim.

claim: The expression of Trissin in two LNds was confirmed.
source: Initially, we confirmed the expression of CCHa1 in two DN1s (Fujiwara et al., 2018), sNFP in four s-LNvs and two LNds (Johard et al., 2009), and Trissin in two LNds (Ma et al., 2021), aligning with previous findings.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to support the claim.

claim: The expression of nAChRα1, nAChRα2, nAChRβ2, GABA-B-R2, CCHa1-R, and Dh31-R in all or subsets of LNvs was identified.
source: Additionally, we identified the expression of nAChRα1, nAChRα2, nAChRβ2, GABA-B-R2, CCHa1-R, and Dh31-R in all or subsets of LNvs, consistent with suggestions from studies using ligands or agonists in LNvs (Duhart et al., 2020; Fujiwara et al., 2018; Lelito and Shafer, 2012; Shafer et al., 2008; Figure 4C and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations and supported by figures.

claim: Approximately five DN1s were positive for Nplp-KI-LexA, indicating a broader expression than previously reported.
source: Regarding previously reported Nplp1 in two DN1as (Shafer et al., 2006), we found approximately five DN1s positive for Nplp-KI-LexA, indicating a broader expression than previously reported.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation.

claim: Four DN1s, four s-LNvs, and two LNds were identified for Dh31-KI-LexA, contrasting with the two DN1s found in immunocytochemical analysis.
source: A similar pattern emerged in our analysis of Dh31-KI-LexA, where four DN1s, four s-LNvs, and two LNds were identified, contrasting with the two DN1s found in immunocytochemical analysis (Goda et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation.

claim: Co-localization analysis of Dh31-KI-LexA and anti-PDF revealed labeling of all PDF-positive s-LNvs but not l-LNvs.
source: Co-localization analysis of Dh31-KI-LexA and anti-PDF revealed labeling of all PDF-positive s-LNvs but not l-LNvs (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A), suggesting that the differences may arise from the broader labeling of 3' end knockin LexA drivers or the amplitude effect of the binary expression system.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a figure showing co-localization.

claim: No stable positive signals for both Pdf and Pdfr were observed in Flp-out intersection experiments.
source: Despite the well-known expression of PDF in LNvs and PDFR in s-LNvs (Shafer et al., 2008), we did not observe stable positive signals for both in Flp-out intersection experiments, although both Pdf-KI-LexA and Pdfr-KI-LexA label LNvs as expected (Figure 4—figure supplement 3B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation and supported by figures.

claim: Knocking out Pdf or Pdfr in clock neurons phenocopied their mutants with lower MAI, advanced evening activity, low power, high arrhythmic rate, and shorter period.
source: Knocking out Pdf or Pdfr in clock neurons phenocopied their mutants with lower MAI, advanced evening activity, low power, high arrhythmic rate, and shorter period (Hyun et al., 2005; Lear et al., 2005; Renn et al., 1999: Supplementary file 6 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations and supported by figures.

claim: The MAI-decreasing phenotype of Dh31 knockout was reproduced in the pilot screen.
source: The MAI-decreasing phenotype of Dh31 knockout was also reproduced in this pilot screen (Goda et al., 2019; Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation.

claim: Leaky expression of Cas9.M9 and sgRNA might have caused disruption of Dh31, Dh44, Pdf, and Pdfr.
source: Unexpectedly, additional experimental replications with full controls using Cas9.M9 revealed that leaky expression of Cas9.M9 and sgRNA might have caused disruption of Dh31, Dh44, Pdf, and Pdfr (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D), which was not suitable for neuronal-specific mutagenesis of some genes.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures.

claim: Only the Pdf and Pdfr clock neuron knockout flies showed positive EAPIs, indicating an advanced evening activity.
source: Only the Pdf and Pdfr clock neuron knockout flies showed positive EAPIs, indicating an advanced evening activity (Supplementary file 6 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures.

claim: nAChRα1, MsR1, mAChR-B, and CNMa cKO flies had the highest MAPI values.
source: nAChRα1, MsR1, mAChR-B, and CNMa cKO flies had the highest MAPI values (Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: CNMa plays a role in regulating morning anticipatory activity.
source: We further confirmed their phenotypes using Cas9.M6, which revealed that CNMa plays a role in regulating morning anticipatory activity (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a figure.

claim: Conditionally knocking out CNMa in clock neurons advanced morning activity and increased MAPI, leaving the power and period intact in male flies.
source: Conditionally knocking out CNMa in clock neurons advanced morning activity (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 2B) and increased MAPI (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and C), leaving the power and period intact in male flies (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing activity and MAPI data.

claim: The same advanced morning activity phenotype was observed in female flies.
source: The same advanced morning activity phenotype was also observed in female flies (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D–G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures.

claim: Both male and female CNMaKO flies exhibited the same phenotypes as seen in the CNMa cKO.
source: Both male and female CNMaKO flies exhibited the same phenotypes as seen in the CNMa cKO (Figure 5G–I).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing activity data.

claim: CNMa expression was found in DN1 neurons.
source: Previous studies have found CNMa expression in DN1 neurons (Abruzzi et al., 2017; Jin et al., 2021; Ma et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to support the claim.

claim: The intersection showed four DN1p and one DN3 CNMa-positive neurons in Clk856-labeled neurons.
source: Our intersection showed four DN1p and one DN3 CNMa-positive neurons in Clk856-labeled neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 2, #16, Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures.

claim: Six pairs of CNMa neurons located in the DN1p region and three pairs located in the subesophageal ganglion (SOG) had the brightest GFP signals.
source: Analysis with an endogenous CNMa-KI-GAL4 knockin driver showed that six pairs of CNMa neurons located in the DN1p region and three pairs located in the subesophageal ganglion (SOG) had the brightest GFP signals (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a figure showing GFP signals.

claim: Dendrites of CNMa neurons were concentrated in DN1p and SOG, with their axons distributed around DN1p region, lateral horn (LH), and prow region (PRW).
source: Dendrites of CNMa neurons were concentrated in DN1p and SOG, with their axons distributed around DN1p region, lateral horn (LH), and prow region (PRW) (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing neuron projections.

claim: Downstream of CNMa neurons were about 15 pairs of neurons in the SOG, 5 pairs of LNd neurons, 1 pair of DN3 neurons, and 6 intercerebralis (PI) neurons.
source: Using the trans-tango strategy (Talay et al., 2017), we also found that downstream of CNMa neurons were about 15 pairs of neurons in the SOG, 5 pairs of LNd neurons, 1 pair of DN3 neurons, and 6 intercerebralis (PI) neurons (Figure 6D, arrowhead).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation and supported by a figure.

claim: Two type I neurons projected to anterior region and four type II neurons had fewer projections to anterior region.
source: We found two arborization patterns: type I with two neurons whose branches projecting to the anterior region, as observed in CNMa∩GMR51H05, CNMa∩Pdfr, and CNMa∩GMR79A11 (Figure 6E, G, and H), and type II with four neurons branching on the posterior side with few projections to the anterior region, as observed in CNMa∩GMR91F02 (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing neuron projections.

claim: CNMa knockout in type I or type II neurons all reproduced the MAPI-increased phenotype of clk856-specific CNMa knockout.
source: CNMa knockout in type I or type II neurons (GMR51H05-GAL4, GMR91F02-GAL4, and GMR79A11-GAL4) all reproduced the MAPI-increased phenotype of clk856-specific CNMa knockout (Figure 6I).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a figure showing MAPI data.

claim: Type II neurons-specific CNMa knockout showed weaker advanced morning activity without advanced morning peak.
source: However, type II neurons-specific CNMa knockout (CNMa ∩ GMR91F02) showed weaker advanced morning activity without advanced morning peak (Figure 6N), while type I neurons-specific CNMa knockout did (Figure 6J), indicating a possibility that these two type I CNMa neurons are the main functional subset regulating the morning anticipation activity of fruit fly.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing activity data.

claim: Type I neurons-specific CNMa knockout showed advanced morning peak.
source: However, type II neurons-specific CNMa knockout (CNMa ∩ GMR91F02) showed weaker advanced morning activity without advanced morning peak (Figure 6N), while type I neurons-specific CNMa knockout did (Figure 6J), indicating a possibility that these two type I CNMa neurons are the main functional subset regulating the morning anticipation activity of fruit fly.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing activity data.

claim: Two type I CNMa neurons are the main functional subset regulating the morning anticipation activity of fruit fly.
source: However, type II neurons-specific CNMa knockout (CNMa ∩ GMR91F02) showed weaker advanced morning activity without advanced morning peak (Figure 6N), while type I neurons-specific CNMa knockout did (Figure 6J), indicating a possibility that these two type I CNMa neurons are the main functional subset regulating the morning anticipation activity of fruit fly.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Two Pdfr and CNMa double-positive DN1ps have a type I projection pattern.
source: We also identified two Pdfr and CNMa double-positive DN1ps, which have a type I projection pattern (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a figure showing neuron projections.

claim: GMR51H05 and GMR79A11 Gal4 drivers could partially rescue the morning anticipation and power phenotype of Pdfr knockout flies to a considerably larger extent than the GMR91F02 driver.
source: Reintroduction of Pdfr in Pdfr knockout background revealed that GMR51H05 and GMR79A11 Gal4 drivers, which covered the main functional CNMa-positive subset, could partially rescue the morning anticipation and power phenotype of Pdfr knockout flies to a considerably larger extent than the GMR91F02 driver (Figure 6Q–S, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A, and Supplementary file 7).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing rescue data.

claim: Knocking out Pdfr by GMR51H05 and CNMa GAL4 decreased morning anticipation of flies.
source: Moreover, knocking out Pdfr by GMR51H05 and CNMa GAL4, which cover type I CNMa neurons, decreased morning anticipation of flies (Figure 6T, Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing activity data.

claim: The decrease in morning anticipation observed in the Pdfr knockout by CNMa-GAL4 was not as pronounced as with GMR51H05-GAL4.
source: However, the decrease in morning anticipation observed in the Pdfr knockout by CNMa-GAL4 was not as pronounced as with GMR51H05-GAL4.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a comparison of experimental results.

claim: There is a possibility that CNMa secretion is regulated by PDF/PDFR signal.
source: Because the presumptive main subset of functional CNMa is also PDFR-positive, there is a possibility that CNMa secretion is regulated by PDF/PDFR signal.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a speculation based on the experimental results.

claim: There is only one CNMa receptor reported in the fly genome.
source: There is only one CNMa receptor reported in the fly genome (Jung et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to support the claim.

claim: CNMaRKO-p65AD knockout showed advanced morning activity and increased MAPI in both sexes.
source: We generated a CNMaRKO-p65AD line by CRISPR/Cas9 (Figure 7A), and this knockout showed advanced morning activity (Figure 7B and D) and increased MAPI (Figure 7C and E) in both sexes.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing activity and MAPI data.

claim: CNMaR expression was observed across the whole brain, especially in DN1p, DN3, the PI, and the SOG.
source: CNMaRKI-Gal4/UAS-mCD8::GFP and CNMaRKI-Gal4/UAS-stinger::Red showed expression of CNMaR across the whole brain (Figure 7F, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), especially in DN1p, DN3, the PI, and the SOG.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing expression patterns.

claim: The dendrite arborization and synaptic projections of CNMaR neurons covered broad regions at the PI, the SOG, the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum (PVLP), and the central complex (CC).
source: The dendrite arborization and synaptic projections of CNMaR neurons also covered broad regions (Figure 7G and H), at the PI, the SOG, the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum (PVLP), and the central complex (CC).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing neuron projections.

claim: cKO of CNMaR in neurons by C-cCCTomics phenocopied CNMaRKO-p65AD phenotype.
source: Further cKO of CNMaR in neurons by C-cCCTomics phenocopied CNMaRKO-p65AD phenotype (Figure 7I–L).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by figures showing activity data.

claim: CNMaR is similar to CNMa in regulating morning anticipation.
source: These results indicate that CNMaR is similar to CNMa in regulating morning anticipation.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the experimental results.
